What makes a model reliable

A model learns patterns from its training data. Evaluate it on separate data to see how well it handles unfamiliar examples. Its errors show where you might need better data or a different model.

From datasets to deployed software

The proposed projects are shown by year. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

  1. Year 1 Programs and data analysis

    Write programs to analyse data and solve practical problems.

  2. Year 2 Machine learning models

    Build and evaluate a model, such as a recommendation engine.

  3. Year 3 Vision and language applications

    Develop software that uses computer vision, language models and generative AI.

  4. Year 4 An AI product for real users

    Put an AI product in users’ hands, then spend a semester in supervised engineering work.

Machine learning, data engineering and deployment

The proposed curriculum starts with Python, data structures, algorithms and mathematics for machine learning. It also covers deep learning, computer vision, language models and generative AI. Study how to prepare data, deploy and monitor models, and develop AI responsibly.

Where it leads

Explore work as an AI or machine learning engineer, data scientist, applied AI engineer or MLOps engineer. The skills also support building an AI startup.

For those who want the detail

MLOps covers what happens when a trained model goes into use. You deploy it, monitor how it performs and maintain it as the data or application changes.

See how AI is used in projects and assessments

Common questions

If AI writes code, why study computer science?

Computer science teaches you to design systems, evaluate the software a tool generates and improve the models that generate it.

Will I learn to deploy a model?

The proposed curriculum includes model deployment and monitoring alongside training and evaluation.

Follow a model from training to use.

Ask an adviser how the proposed projects teach you to evaluate predictions and turn a model into working software.
